title: AI-Powered Active Directory Risk Profiling and Network Security Monitoring System
technologies: Windows Server AD, Python, Flask/FastAPI, SQLite
evidence: NOC operations, cloud IAM and the ML cyber-attack detection portfolio
summary: Create a controlled AD lab, collect Windows events and turn rule-based findings into user and asset risk profiles.
modules: Configure test users, groups and Windows event collection
Store timestamped events and implement explainable risk rules
Build authenticated dashboards, event filters and exportable reports
caveat: Agree the monitored event IDs and lab resources first. AI explanations must remain tied to collected evidence; this is a laboratory monitoring project.
validation: Test failed logins, account changes, access permissions and collector failure. Compare dashboard findings with the original Windows events.

title: AI-Based Sentiment and Emotion Analysis of Text Using Natural Language Processing
summary: Classify sentiment and emotion in submitted text, with prediction history, confidence information and evaluation charts.
modules: Prepare labelled sentiment and emotion datasets
Compare TF-IDF classification baselines and evaluate each label
Connect manual text and batch input to a results dashboard
caveat: Check dataset licences, label definitions and language coverage before training. Confidence scores need careful interpretation and do not establish a person’s actual emotional state.
validation: Keep test records separate from preprocessing and training. Report per-class precision, recall, F1 and examples of misclassified text.

title: Fake News Detection System
evidence: text classification and machine-learning evaluation experience
summary: Compare text classifiers that label news as potentially fake or potentially genuine and explain the limits of those predictions.
modules: Clean and deduplicate article titles and bodies
Compare Logistic Regression, Multinomial Naive Bayes and SVM using TF-IDF
Present confusion matrices, model comparisons and error analysis
caveat: The brief specifies a Python classification application. A Flask interface would be an additional scope choice, not a stated requirement. Predictions do not independently verify facts.
validation: Split data before fitting the vectorizer. Examine duplicate leakage and changes in predictions caused by punctuation, spacing and publication topics.

title: ExamPredict - Intelligent Student Performance Prediction and Early Warning System
evidence: Flask REST integration and applied machine-learning projects
summary: Predict examination scores and compare Linear Regression with Random Forest Regression through a Flask analytics application.
modules: Prepare academic and study-habit inputs with a reproducible split
Implement prediction, model-comparison, history and metrics endpoints
Display estimated scores, instructor-defined risk levels and study suggestions
caveat: The brief describes a synthetic student dataset. Results demonstrate a modelling workflow and cannot establish real student outcomes.
validation: Compare MAE, RMSE and R-squared on held-out data. Verify input ranges and ensure prediction uses the fitted training preprocessing pipeline.

title: GraduPredict Graduate Placement Prediction System
technologies: Python, Streamlit, SQLite, pandas, NumPy, openpyxl
evidence: Python classification, dashboards and data processing
summary: Estimate placement readiness using Logistic Regression and a shallow Decision Tree, with individual and teacher batch predictions.
modules: Implement student and teacher permissions
Validate Excel uploads with at least three student records
Compare decision thresholds, model disagreement and exported results
caveat: Streamlit is an adjacent framework to the demonstrated Flask experience. Placement estimates are advisory and must not be presented as employment guarantees.
validation: Test batch column validation, invalid values and cross-user access. Measure classification performance and investigate threshold sensitivity.

title: Rule-Based Student Academic Advising and Course Recommendation System
evidence: Flask applications, access control and relational database workflows
summary: Turn explicit academic rules into explainable course-load recommendations that can be reviewed and approved.
modules: Model course prerequisites and student academic inputs
Implement eligibility checks, course prioritization and explanations
Build the student-entry and approval workflow
caveat: This is a rule-based system. Confirm the university’s actual advising rules instead of substituting an ML model or invented academic policy.
validation: Use cases should cover blocked prerequisites, course-load boundaries, conflicting inputs and approval permissions. Trace each recommendation to its rule.

title: TopicTrace: Concept-Level Learning Gap Detector and Adaptive Revision Planner
technologies: Python, scikit-learn, XGBoost, SHAP, Flask/Django, SQL
evidence: Python analytics and explainable prediction dashboards
summary: Use assessment evidence to identify concept-level learning gaps and produce an explained revision plan.
modules: Map questions and assessment outcomes to concepts
Prepare model features and explained learning-gap alerts
Show revision priorities and teacher-facing analytics
caveat: Topic-level recommendations depend on correctly tagged assessment data. XGBoost and SHAP are extensions of the demonstrated ML stack and need an initial feasibility check.
validation: Hold out evaluation records, review explanation stability and check that weak concepts lead to relevant revision activities rather than generic advice.

title: SMART-EDU: An AI-Based Early Academic Warning and Personalized Learning Recommendation System
technologies: Python, pandas, scikit-learn Decision Tree, Streamlit
evidence: Python machine-learning pipelines and dashboard development
summary: Use pre-midterm information to estimate academic risk and connect topic-tagged assessment results with learning recommendations.
modules: Prepare historical pre-midterm inputs and actual midterm labels
Train and evaluate a Decision Tree baseline
Display early warnings and topic-based support suggestions
caveat: Historical outcomes and topic-tagged assessments are needed for different parts of the system. Streamlit is an adjacent framework; data availability is the first feasibility check.
validation: Exclude outcome-derived features from prediction inputs. Validate the warning threshold and verify that recommendations correspond to the assessed topic gaps.

title: Crop Data Processing and Analytical Reporting System for Pakistan
technologies: Python, PostgreSQL, pandas, SQLAlchemy/psycopg, Streamlit, Plotly
evidence: Python automation, data validation and database-backed applications
summary: Build a reproducible crop-data ingestion and reporting pipeline with explicit mapping, observation keys and transaction behaviour.
modules: Read source CSV fields as text and validate configured mappings
Implement observation keys, numeric parsing and database transactions
Expose analytical reports through a local Streamlit interface
caveat: PostgreSQL ETL and Streamlit extend the existing Python foundation. Follow the supplied input contract; do not replace it with an external AI service or assume large-scale performance from a small sample.
validation: Test malformed numeric values, duplicate observations, reruns and rollback on invalid records. Reconcile report totals with the accepted source rows.

title: Smart English Text Error Detection and Correction System
evidence: NLP pipelines and Python web application experience
summary: Detect English writing errors, let users review individual corrections and export corrected documents while preserving paragraph order.
modules: Accept text and DOCX input with safe validation
Classify writing errors and show explanations and suggestions
Apply accepted corrections and generate a corrected DOCX
caveat: LanguageTool integration and document processing need a prototype. Preserve the original text so users can inspect every suggested change.
validation: Test accepted and rejected edits, overlapping suggestions, punctuation and multi-paragraph documents. Compare exported text order against the source.

title: Student Fee and Scholarship Management System Using Python
evidence: Python programming, data modelling and access-control workflows
summary: Manage student fees, scholarship adjustments, instalments, receipts and outstanding balances in a desktop application.
modules: Model students, departments, fee structures and scholarships
Implement accountant, administrator and student access
Calculate balances and create receipts and collection reports
caveat: The brief requires a Tkinter desktop application, not a Flask website. Tkinter is an adjacent skill; prototype the GUI and printing workflow before committing to delivery.
validation: Check scholarship percentages, late fines, partial payments and repeated receipt actions. Use decimal arithmetic and reconcile every balance with payment history.

title: Simulation-Based Web Application for Visualization and Comparative Analysis of Disk Scheduling Algorithms
evidence: Python logic, Flask interfaces and technical visualization
summary: Visualize disk-head movement and compare scheduling algorithms using consistent request queues and seek-distance calculations.
modules: Validate request queues, disk bounds and initial head position
Implement the algorithms required by the approved brief
Plot movement and compare results with worked examples
caveat: Algorithm correctness is central. Confirm direction and boundary conventions for each algorithm before drawing comparisons; the tool list alone does not define the required implementation.
validation: Use hand-calculated cases, repeated requests, empty queues and disk-edge positions. Verify reported total movement against the plotted head path.

title: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis on E-Commerce Reviews
summary: Extract product aspects and classify sentiment toward each aspect instead of assigning one label to an entire review.
modules: Establish an aspect-labelled dataset and baseline
Implement aspect extraction and compare sentiment models
Build CSV review upload and aspect-level charts
caveat: Transformer fine-tuning and sequence labelling go beyond the demonstrated baseline. Confirm dataset access through the student’s VU account and available compute before accepting the full scope.
validation: Evaluate extraction and sentiment separately. Include reviews that praise one aspect while criticizing another and report per-aspect errors.

title: SmartAssist: AI-Powered Help Desk and Ticket Support System
technologies: PHP 8, Laravel, MySQL, AI API, Bootstrap
evidence: support operations, REST integration and authentication concepts
summary: Connect knowledge-based AI support with ticket escalation, support-agent replies and resolution tracking.
modules: Model ticket lifecycle, permissions and knowledge-base records
Review AI integration and human escalation behaviour
Define analytics, validation and API troubleshooting checks
caveat: The official backend is PHP 8 with Laravel. The portfolio demonstrates Python/Flask rather than Laravel; offer requirements, API and debugging guidance only unless that skill gap is resolved.
validation: Test role separation, ticket ownership, unhelpful AI responses, escalation and status transitions. Confirm users can reach a human when automated support fails.

title: AI-Powered Smart Job Portal with Resume Screening and Career Guidance
technologies: PHP, MySQL, Python NLP service, REST API
evidence: Python NLP and REST integration experience
summary: Extract resume information, compare candidates with job descriptions and provide explainable match scores through a Python service.
modules: Define resume parsing and skills-normalization contracts
Develop and evaluate matching and missing-skill explanations
Review the REST boundary between the PHP portal and Python service
caveat: The brief requires a PHP/MySQL portal plus a separate Python AI service. Python/NLP support fits the portfolio; full PHP delivery needs additional demonstrated capability.
validation: Test missing resume fields, malformed files and scoring consistency. Treat match scores as decision support and check for unjustified ranking differences.
